items.stem: What is melted rock called while it is still inside the Earth?
items.explanation: Magma is melted rock material inside the Earth that contains dissolved gas. Once it reaches the surface, it is called lava.

items.stem: What is melted rock called once it reaches the Earth's surface?
items.explanation: On the surface, melted rock is called lava. The same material is called magma while it is still underground.

items.stem: Which volcano is the tallest, with steep sides and the most violent, deadly eruptions?
items.explanation: Composite volcanoes are the tallest, with steep sides and a broad base. Their thick lava traps gas, making them the most violent and deadly.

items.stem: Mauna Loa has broad, gently sloping sides and erupts without violent explosions. Which type of volcano is it?
items.explanation: Mauna Loa is a shield volcano. Thin, runny lava flows out many times and spreads in wide layers, building broad, gentle slopes.

items.stem: Why does a shield volcano have gentle slopes and calm eruptions?

options.text: Its thick, sticky lava traps gas underground
Its thin, runny lava flows easily and spreads out
It has no magma chamber to feed it
It is made only of ash and no lava

items.explanation: Shield volcanoes are built by thin, low-viscosity lava. Gas escapes easily, so the lava flows quietly and spreads into broad, gentle slopes.

items.stem: Why do composite volcanoes erupt so violently?

options.text: Thick lava traps gas, so pressure builds until it explodes
Thin lava lets all the gas escape gently
They sit on top of cold, solid rock
They are too small to erupt at all

items.explanation: Composite volcanoes have thick, high-viscosity lava that traps gas. Pressure builds until it bursts free in a violent, explosive eruption.

items.stem: Which is the smallest type of volcano, usually under 1,000 feet, built from cinders that pile up around a vent?
items.explanation: A cinder cone is the smallest volcano, with a very steep cone shape. It is built from small pieces of lava that pile up around the vent.

items.stem: How does a cinder cone form?

options.text: Runny lava flows out and spreads in wide, flat sheets
Thick lava and ash build up in alternating layers over time
The magma chamber slowly cools without ever erupting
Erupted bits of lava cool in the air and pile up around the vent

items.explanation: A cinder cone forms when small pieces of lava erupt, cool in the air, and fall back down around the vent, building a steep cone.

items.stem: What property of lava best explains the difference between gentle and explosive eruptions?

options.text: How thick or thin (viscous) the lava is
The time of day the volcano erupts
The size of the crater at the top

items.explanation: Viscosity, how thick or runny the lava is, controls whether gas escapes or gets trapped, which decides if an eruption is gentle or explosive.

items.stem: Mount St. Helens (a composite volcano) and Mauna Loa (a shield volcano) are both volcanoes, yet they look and erupt very differently. What best explains this?

options.text: One is a real volcano and the other is not
They are made of completely different elements than rock
Differences in lava thickness and trapped gas lead to different eruption styles and shapes
Shield volcanoes are younger, so they are unable to explode

items.explanation: Both are fed by magma, but the viscosity of their lava differs. Thick lava traps gas and builds steep, explosive composite volcanoes; thin lava flows gently and builds broad shield volcanoes.
